title: Stability gatekeeper for quant rollouts with synthetic anchors and pass/fail profiling
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Build an automated validation harness (gatekeeper) that evaluates candidate quant profiles (FP8/INT8) against a reference (FP32) using a mix of curated "golden" prompts and synthetic anchor prompts. The harness should output a deterministic pass/fail decision plus a rich diagnostics bundle to help engineers tune calibration and quant profiles. Key functions: (1) corpus curation + stratified sampling (domain, length, interaction type); (2) activation collection and static calibration options (per-layer static ranges, per-channel where available) and dynamic calibration fallback; (3) batched golden replay comparing baseline and quant variant outputs; (4) metric suite (semantic embedding cosine, token-level KL, per-token logit-delta, EM/answer-match for closed QA, ROUGE-L/ BLEU-like overlap for generation, and latency/memory deltas); (5) composite gating policy with weighted thresholds and per-cohort fail isolation; (6) CI integration to block / mark canary on PRs and model rollouts if thresholds fail; (7) auto-suggestions for quant profile adjustments (e.g., widen scale for top-k sensitive layers, apply bias-correction for layernorm drift). The harness must be usable offline for scheduled acceptance runs and in CI for PR-level checks. Output artifacts: per-run CSV, JSON summary, PDF human report, and links to recording of failing examples in internal Drive.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end run reproduces FP32 vs FP8/INT8 comparison for a supplied model and quant profile
Composite pass/fail decision produced and persisted to artifacts store
Human-readable PDF report with top 50 failing prompts and per-layer sensitivity table
CI integration that fails build when candidate profile fails gate for P0 profiles
Suggested corrective actions included in report for failed layers or cohorts
approach: 1) Assemble golden corpus: 2.5k prompts stratified across product intents, edge cases, and adversarially-generated anchors. 2) Implement a synthetic anchor generator to create perturbations for each golden prompt (token drop/insert, prefix shift, context truncation) to stress quant edge cases. 3) Calibration: collect activation histograms on N=512 calibration samples; support both static min-max, percentile (99.99th), and MSE-based per-channel scale search. 4) Run batched replay: baseline FP32 vs candidate quant profile in identical runtime settings (same seeds, streaming disabled for deterministic comparison). 5) Compute metrics: embedding cosine (use sentence-embedding model), token-KL, mean absolute logit-delta, EM for QA, ROUGE-L for long-form; normalize deltas by token length and aggregate with weights {semantic:0.5, token-kl:0.25, em:0.15, rouge:0.1}. 6) Gate: pass if composite delta < 0.02 and no cohort exceeds individual metric thresholds (semantic delta < 0.03, token-KL < 0.04, EM drop < 1.0% absolute). 7) Produce diagnostics: layer-saliency heatmap, per-prompt exemplar, and prioritized actionable list. 8) Expose a CLI and REST endpoint for programmatic runs and a GitHub Actions workflow for PR-level checks.
design_decisions: Use stratified sampling rather than purely random sampling to ensure coverage across intents and lengths
Weight semantic similarity higher than token-level metrics to better reflect end-user perceived quality
Require deterministic replay (fixed seeds, same beam/temperature) to make diffs interpretable
Run calibration offline with an option to re-calibrate during canary if minor deltas are observed
Keep the composite gate conservative for production profiles and more permissive for experimental profiles
risks: False positives from brittle golden prompts that over-emphasize token-level matching
Under-estimating rare-context failures because calibration sample set is too small
High CI cost if full 2.5k prompt suite runs on every PR — need tiered quick checks
Model non-determinism (e.g., hardware variance) causing spurious failures — require control experiments
Suggestions may not always be actionable for model families that interact poorly with per-channel quant
